angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 712,049 km at 148.13 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.7508 +/- 0.0127 mas (same row, RUWE 0.92): 148.13 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.0235 +/- 0.018 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1386 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 712,049 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.0363 +/- 0.0349 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1386 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5735 +/- 75 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1386 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1386 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1386.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.433, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
